newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - March 14.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The chief justice of the Criminal Court is to explain to the United States ambassador today the decision of his deputy to release a suspected international heroin trafficker. Pradit Ekmanee, who is to meet William Itoh at the court, will also spell out the punishment Somchai Udomwong could expect if he was found to have acted dishonestly in releasing Li Yun-chung on bail. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has instructed the Counter Corruption Commission (CCC) to launch a new investigation into alleged large-scale VAT fraud which took place during the Chuan Leekpai government and to leave no stone unturned in searching for the culprits. Chavalit's instruction is politically significant since the VAT investigation could generate a backlash on the Democrat Party, his main rival. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- The superintendent of Mae Hong Son's Salween National Park has been transferred following revelations that trees in the park were illegally cut down, shipped across the river to Burma and then imported by Thai companies. The Royal Forestry Department will set up an investigative committee to determine whether park chief, Jaen Thafong, is guilty of participating in the illegal timber trade. (THE NATION)

- The rehabilitation process for the ailing Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) will move ahead next month following the approval by the Bank of Thailand (BOT) of new management proposals from the Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand (IFCT). BOT Governor says IFCT has assured the central bank's financial arm, the Rehabilitation Fund for Financial Institutions that the first year of manangement would be a profitable one. (BUSINESS DAY, BANGKOK POST)

- Thailand and Burma have signed a 30-year contract for the Yetagun Gas Sales Agreement, based on an initial reserve base of 1.1 trillion cubic feet of natural gas. The supply should be on-stream by late 1999, and is expected to be able to satisfy the rising demand for energy in Thailand. (BUSINESS DAY, BANGKOK POST)

- National carrier Thai Airways International is to form one of the world's largest aviation partnerships with four other airlines in May. According to the plan, THAI, United Airlines, Germany-based Lufthansa, Scandinavian Airlines and Air Canada will sign a non-binding memorandum of understanding on May 14 in Frankfurt. The pact will create a network which will cover five continents and help THAI regain its competitiveness in the world market. (THE NATION)
